Testimony of Anya Trundy, Deputy Commissioner Department of Administrative and Financial Sen/ices
I
Testifying in Favor
LD 2138, Resolve, Authorizing the Department of Administrative and Financial Services to Convey the Interests of the State in Certain Real Property in Bangor
Presented by Sen. Joseph Baldacci
To the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government
Representative Salisbury and members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and
Local Government, I am Anya Trundy, Deputy Commissioner for the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. l am providing testimony in support of LD 2138,
which would permit the State of convey the Elizabeth Levinson Center in Bangorto United Cerebral Palsy of Northeastern Maine.
Since 2009, the Elizabeth Levinson Center has been a base of operations for the UCP. This non-profit organization is dedicated to advancing the independence, productivity and full citizenship of people with disabilities, supporting individuals and families in Maine with respect, dedication and a community-oriented vision.
The facility itself, a single-story brick structure on an 8.67 acre plot of land, is owned by the State and leased to UCP. The need for improvements to the building has grown steadily over the years, and now there are major repairs and maintenance which must take place. The Levinson Center is not used for State purposes, and the list of other
capital improvements which require immediate attention is long. UCP, alternatively, is both willing and able to undertake these investments in the property, which will be a great benefit to their operations; however, the terms of the lease with the State prove to be a barrier to them pursuing these improvements.
LD 2138 removes this barrier by transferring ownership of the building to UCP with a long-
term ground lease. This ground lease, which would extend for 50 to 75 years, would allow the State to retain ownership of the property on which the building is located, while
granting UCP the ability to secure loans and engage in the needed improvements to the
building.
UCP and the State have maintained a positive and constructive relationship for years,
and this bill will give them the space to continue to grow and improve their organization and its functions.
I urge you to support LD 2138. I am happy to answer questions and will be available at the work
session.

Testimony of Scott Tash, Chief Executive Officer

In Support of LD 2138
Resolve, Authorizing the Department of Administrative and Financial Services to Convey the Interests of the State in Certain Real Property in Bangor
Committee on State and Local Government January 28, 2026
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and members of the Committee on State
and Local Government,
My name is Scott Tash, and I am the CEO at UCP of Maine. UCP of Maine has been serving adults,
children and families with a wide range of intellectual disabilities, mental health disorders, behavioral challenges and/or physical challenges since 1954, and those services currently include operating an Intermediate Care Facility in Bangor for individuals with significant developmental and medical needs,
generally known as the Elizabeth Levinson Center, located at 159 Hogan Rd. I am pleased to offer this testimony in support of LD 2138 on behalf of my organization, UCP of Maine.
l want to thank Senator Baldacci for sponsoring this bill and the staff of the Department of Finance and Administration for the collaboration and open discussions around the needs of our program, the facility upgrades, and the importance of long-term planning.
Since 2009, UCP of Maine has operated the Elizabeth Levinson Center, leasing the building from the
State. During this time, we have enjoyed a very collaborative relationship, with UCP providing
maintenance and capital upgrades as needed to the Elizabeth Levinson Center building along the way.
Some of the previous projects we have collaborated with the Bureau of General Services on include a
Boiler upgrade, front and rear parking lot paving, and installation of a full facility generator. While the building has remained in compliance with all codes and standards throughout the duration of the lease, and received favorable comments during successful licensing review and fire marshal inspections, it does continue to age and there will be significant capital investments needed in the near and short term, specifically a critical roof replacement that has been discussed for some time.
As the Intermediate Care Facility program operates on a cost basis, essentially a "break-even" for the year, it is nearly impossible to build reserves to draw from in order to fund large capital projects,
therefore requiring support from financial partners. Over the years when investing in the facility, we
have been fortunate to have support from our financial partners, as they understand the importance of
the service we provide and the relationship we have with the State. However, without equity or interest in the building, this becomes ihcreasingly challenging, particularly when evaluating larger scale needs.

Aging facilities are not new issues for the State, or for us as an organization. And continued investment in those facilities is critical in the ability to successfully provide CMS certified programs into the future. Substantial and critical investments of the property at 159 Hogan Rd, Bangor, and the conveyance of the building to UCP of Maine will allow those investments to proceed in a timely manner. I support and urge
you to authorize the Department of Finance and Administration to convey such interests to avoid disruption to the critical services the residents of the Elizabeth Levinson Center need and deserve.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.
Respectfully Submitted,
Scott D. Tash, CEO UCP of Maine
Scott.tash@ucpofmaine.org
